items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I don't mean what is normally called Chicago jazz, like Jimmy McPartland and those guys.

ctx.x: Well, at one time there may -- at one time I think there was. But I think most of the jazz today is just like if you go to New Orleans, you find -- you can find the same kind of jazz you find in Chicago or New York or anywhere. But they stick to their tradition. But Chicago had -- not now --
I don't mean what is normally called Chicago jazz, like Jimmy McPartland and those guys. I don't mean that.

items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: I had some tunes and things, and I asked Jimmy if he wanted to make a session with us and he did.

ctx.x: This was 195-- around -- see, because when I put that 'Hambone' out, that was in 1952. See, so in -- pardon me, this was during that time. So we -- I had some tunes and things, and I asked Jimmy if he wanted to make a session with us and he did. And that was -- and then, in the club, every day the thing that really set him off, well, this is where he created it, right there in the club. That was his big thing, that was his --
